text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All newspapers lead with fighting in Cambodia, in which Cambodian strong man Hun Sen says he has ousted his rival, Prince Norodom Ranriddh.
-- Malaysia Airlines has suspended all flights to Phnom Penh until Thursday following the closure of the Pochentong international airport due to the political violence there.

-- Although the Cabinet has approved the ticket charges of all types of sports for the KL '98 Commonwealth Games, the Games' Cabinet committee head Muhyiddin Yassin, concerned about crowd turnout, has called for a review of the rates.
-- The captain of the Lunntu ship detained for spilling oil in the Straits of Malacca near Klang has been ordered to post a 150,000 ringgit bank guarantee for release of the ship.

-- Petrol kiosk operators in the Kuala Lumpur area appear to benefit more from the self-service concept instead of the public, said Domestic Trade and Consumers Affairs Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob. He said the concept has not resulted in cheaper fuel although operations costs have been reduced.

-- Malaysia, which has not requested for Japanese aid since 1995, managed to lessen its dependence on foreign aid and borrowings because it succeeded in involving the private sector in the provision of infrastructure, a report said.
-- Utama Banking Group Bhd is working towards becoming "your friendly one-stop financial centre", providing all the financial services that a customer needs or can think of.
-- The rising world demand for petrochemical products promises a bright future for Petronas' downstream activities and the heavy investment made by the national oil corporation is paying off.
-- Petronas is expected to announce a threshold $10 billion revenue for the year to March 31, 1997, according to sources. The company is scheduled to announce its results next Monday.
